post_title: How many dengue cases will Singapore's NEA report for the epidemiological week ending Saturday 24 October 2026?

question.title: How many dengue cases will Singapore's NEA report for the epidemiological week ending Saturday 24 October 2026?
question.description:
Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) publishes weekly and daily counts of reported dengue cases on its dengue cases page (https://www.nea.gov.sg/dengue-zika/dengue/dengue-cases). Weekly figures are organised by epidemiological week ("E-week"), running Sunday through Saturday. Dengue is endemic in Singapore, with a typical peak transmission season from roughly May to October driven by warmer temperatures and Aedes mosquito activity.

As of the update dated 16 October 2026, recent weekly reported-case counts were: E-week 35 (30 Aug–5 Sep) = 87; E-week 36 = 73; E-week 37 (13–19 Sep) = 74; E-week 38 (20–26 Sep) = 82; E-week 39 (27 Sep–3 Oct) = 71; E-week 40 (4–10 Oct) = 79. The cumulative total for 2026 through the first 40 E-weeks stood at 2,643 cases, running roughly 70% above the same period in 2025. The week ending 10 October (79 cases) was up 8 from the prior week. The E-week ending Saturday 24 October 2026 (E-week 42) is expected to be published around 27–28 October 2026. Note that the most recent weeks' counts are provisional and typically revised slightly upward as late-reported cases are added, so the figure displayed just a few days after the week closes may be lower than the eventual settled count.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the number of weekly reported dengue cases for the epidemiological week (E-week) ending Saturday 24 October 2026, as shown on the National Environment Agency (NEA) dengue cases page (https://www.nea.gov.sg/dengue-zika/dengue/dengue-cases) under the "No. of reported cases" weekly chart/table for that E-week. The value is read as of 23:59 Singapore Time (SGT, UTC+8) on October 29, 2026. For example, if NEA shows 64 cases for that week, this question resolves as 64.
question.fine_print: NEA's weekly figures are provisional and may be revised upward as late-reported cases are added; the figure displayed for the E-week ending 24 October 2026 as of the stated read time governs resolution, regardless of later revision. If the NEA page does not display a value for that specific E-week by the read time, resolution waits until NEA publishes it. If NEA permanently ceases publishing weekly dengue case counts, the question is annulled.
